texts: At a redo CABG, a diseased but patent old vein graft to the LAD is left in place and the LIMA is added to the LAD.
Handling or removing an atherosclerotic vein graft can shower debris into the coronary bed and cause a perioperative infarction.
The LIMA gives the best long-term patency, and the old graft keeps supplying flow while the LIMA takes over.
A new vein graft gives up the survival benefit of the mammary artery.
Removing the old graft adds the embolic risk for no benefit.
In the picture, the crumbling sapphire chain is roped off and Sanji ties the fresh lima vine beside it.
Memory hook: do not touch the old chain; add the living vine.
